subject: math
title: Measuring Angles: Protractors, Reflex Angles, Clockwise and Counterclockwise
seo_title: Grade 6 Measuring Angles Worksheets: Protractor and Reflex Angles (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Use a protractor to measure and construct angles up to 360°, and state the relationship between angles that are measured clockwise and those that are measured counterclockwise
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on measuring angles for the Ontario curriculum: name acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex angles, read both protractor scales, find reflex angles and see why clockwise and counterclockwise angles add up to 360°. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to 360°.
key_sub: Read the protractor scale that starts at 0 on your arm, then check your estimate: acute is less than 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, reflex is between 180° and 360°. For a reflex angle, measure the other side and subtract from 360°.
body_html:
Angle names

An angle is an amount of turn between two arms. We measure it in degrees (°). A full turn is 360°, a straight angle (half a turn) is 180° and a right angle (a quarter turn) is 90°.

NameSize
Acute angleless than 90°
Right angleexactly 90°
Obtuse anglemore than 90°, less than 180°
Straight angleexactly 180°
Reflex anglemore than 180°, less than 360°

Read a protractor

1. Estimate first: acute or obtuse? 2. Put the centre of the protractor on the vertex. 3. Line up one arm with 0. 4. Read the scale that starts at 0 on that arm. 5. Check the reading against your estimate.

Reflex angles

A protractor only goes to 180°. To measure a reflex angle, measure the angle on the other side of the arms, then subtract from 360°.

Measure a reflex angle

The gap on the other side of a reflex angle measures 130°. Find the reflex angle.

The two angles make a full turn: 360° − 130° = 230°.

Answer: 230°

Construct a reflex angle

Construct an angle of 250°.

360° − 250° = 110°. Construct 110° with the protractor, then mark the angle around the outside.

Answer: the outside of a 110° angle

Clockwise and counterclockwise

From one arm you can turn to the other arm two ways: clockwise (the way clock hands move) or counterclockwise (the other way). Together the two turns make a full turn, so they add up to 360°.

Find the other turn

A robot turns 120° counterclockwise. What clockwise turn ends in the same direction?

The two turns add up to 360°: 360° − 120° = 240°.

Answer: 240° clockwise

On a protractor, the inner scale counts counterclockwise from 0 on the right, and the outer scale counts clockwise from 0 on the left.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong scale (140° for a 40° angle)Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm, then check your estimate
Calling 190° obtuseObtuse is between 90° and 180°. More than 180° is reflex
Subtracting from 180° to find a reflex angleA reflex angle and the angle on the other side add up to 360°
Thinking clockwise and counterclockwise angles add up to 180°Between the same two arms they make a full turn: 360°

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about angles in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: They use a protractor to measure and construct angles up to 360°, including reflex angles, and learn that the clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to 360°.

faq.q: How do you measure a reflex angle with a protractor?
faq.a: A protractor only goes to 180°, so measure the angle on the other side of the arms and subtract it from 360°. For example, if the other side is 70°, the reflex angle is 290°.

faq.q: Why do protractors have two scales?
faq.a: So you can measure from an arm on either side: the inner scale counts counterclockwise from 0 on the right, and the outer scale counts clockwise from 0 on the left. Always read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm.

faq.q: Are angles on the Grade 6 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: Yes, spatial sense, including angles, is part of the Grade 6 Ontario math curriculum that EQAO assesses. Practise estimating first, reading the correct protractor scale and finding reflex angles.

items.q: An angle measures 89°. What is its name?
items.e: 89° is less than 90°, so it is acute (only just). A right angle is exactly 90°.

items.q: An angle measures 185°. What is its name?
items.e: 185° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex, even though it is close to a straight angle.

items.q: An angle measures 175°. What is its name?
items.e: 175° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse. It is close to a straight angle, but not 180°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

items.q: Liam says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is he right?
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

items.q: How many degrees are in a full turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°. It is 4 right angles: 4 × 90° = 360°. 180° is a straight angle, only half a turn.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 70°.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
items.e: Acute is less than 90°, right is 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, straight is 180° and reflex is between 180° and 360°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a full turn: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes around the outside. This angle is 320°. (The gap between the arms is 40°, but the arc marks the big angle around the outside.)

items.q: Which list has only reflex angles?
items.e: Reflex angles are more than 180° and less than 360°. 200°, 270° and 345° all fit. 100°, 150° and 175° are obtuse, 180° is straight and 45° is acute.

items.q: An angle measures 270°. What is its name?
items.e: 270° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex. It is three right angles: 3 × 90° = 270°.

items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°, a quarter turn. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its size or its name.

items.q: What is the size of the angle?
items.e: The bottom arm is on 0 at the right, so read the inner scale. It counts counterclockwise from 0 on the right. The other arm crosses it at 110. The outer scale says 70 there, but it counts from the other side. The angle is bigger than a right angle, so 110° makes sense.

items.q: Amira measures an angle and writes 40°. The angle is clearly obtuse. What should she have written?
items.e: An obtuse angle is more than 90°. Amira read the wrong scale: the other scale gives 180° − 40° = 140°.

in the middle of an arm
items.e: The centre goes on the vertex, where the two arms meet. Then line up one arm with 0.

items.q: Ethan wanted to construct an angle of 50°. His base arm is on 0 of the inner scale. The picture shows what he drew. What angle did he actually draw?
items.e: Read the inner scale, because the base arm is on its 0: the second arm is at 130, so the angle is 130°. Ethan used 50 on the outer scale by mistake. 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: Lucas wanted to construct an angle of 70°. His base arm is on 0 of the outer scale. The picture shows what he drew. What angle did he actually draw?
items.e: The base arm is on 0 of the outer scale, so read the outer scale: the second arm is at 110, so the angle is 110°. Lucas used 70 on the inner scale by mistake. 180° − 70° = 110°.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 20 and the other is at 95. The angle is the difference: 95° − 20° = 75°.

items.q: Ava measures an angle that is clearly smaller than a right angle. The arm crosses the protractor at 35 and 145. What is the angle?
items.e: An angle smaller than a right angle is acute, less than 90°, so it is 35°. 145 is on the other scale.

items.q: A reflex angle is 200°. How big is the angle on the other side of its arms?
items.e: The two angles make a full turn: 360° − 200° = 160°. (20° comes from 200° − 180°.)
The two angles go all the way around the vertex, so they add up to 360°. 360° − 40° = 320°. (140° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: The gap between the arms of a reflex angle is 45°. How big is the reflex angle?
A protractor only goes to 180°. How can you construct a reflex angle of 250°?
c: Draw 70°, then mark the angle outside it
Draw 110°, then mark the angle outside it
items.e: 360° − 250° = 110°. Construct an angle of 110°. The angle around the outside is then 250°. (70° comes from 250° − 180°, but the two angles must make a full turn, 360°.)

items.q: An angle is three right angles plus 20°. How big is it?
items.e: Three right angles are 3 × 90° = 270°. 270° + 20° = 290°, a reflex angle. (110° is 90° + 20°.)

items.q: The marked angle between the hands at 4 o’clock is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands make a full turn: 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from 180° − 120°.)

items.q: The protractor measures the angle between the two arms. What is the reflex angle between the same arms?
items.e: The left arm is on 0 of the outer scale, so the angle is 50°. The reflex angle is 360° − 50° = 310°. (230° comes from reading 130 on the wrong scale: 360° − 130° = 230°.)
The two angles go all the way around the vertex, so they add up to 360°. 360° − 155° = 205°. (25° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: To construct a reflex angle of 300°, which angle should you draw first with the protractor?
items.e: The two angles around the vertex make a full turn: 360°. 360° − 300° = 60°. Draw 60°, then mark the big angle around the outside. (120° comes from 300° − 180°.)

items.q: Noah says the reflex angle is 120° when the gap between the arms is 60°, because 180° − 60° = 120°. Is he right?
items.e: A reflex angle is more than 180°, so 120° cannot be right. The two angles make a full turn: 360° − 60° = 300°.

items.q: To find a reflex angle, Kai measures the angle on the other side. It is 130°. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: The two angles go all the way around the vertex, so they make a full turn: 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: The protractor measures the angle between the two arms. What is the reflex angle between the same arms?
items.e: On the inner scale the angle is 75°. The reflex angle goes the other way around. Together they make a full turn: 360° − 75° = 285°. (105° is the reading on the wrong scale.)

items.q: A reflex angle is 3 times as big as the angle on the other side of its arms. How big is the reflex angle?
items.e: The two angles make 4 equal parts of 360°: 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. The reflex angle is 3 × 90° = 270°. (135° comes from sharing 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: Another way to construct 215°: draw a straight angle (180°), then add more. How much more?
items.e: 215° − 180° = 35°. Draw a straight line through the vertex, then measure 35° more past it. (145° is 360° − 215°, the angle on the other side.)

items.q: The counterclockwise angle between two arms is 80°. Leah says the clockwise angle is 100°, because they add up to 180°. Is she right?
items.e: Clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same arms add up to 360°, not 180°. 360° − 80° = 280°.

items.q: The arrow shows a turn from one arm to the other. Which describes the turn?
items.e: The arrow turns the same way as the hands of a clock, so it is clockwise. It turns less than a right angle: about 60°. The counterclockwise angle between the same arms would be about 300°.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 are three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°, a reflex angle. (90° is the counterclockwise turn from 12 to 9.)

items.q: Chloe faces east. She turns 270° counterclockwise. Which way is she facing now?
items.e: Counterclockwise goes east → north → west → south. 270° is three quarter turns, so Chloe ends up facing south. (It is the same as 90° clockwise.)

items.q: A turn of 90° clockwise ends in the same place as a counterclockwise turn of …
items.e: The two turns add up to 360°. 360° − 90° = 270° counterclockwise.

items.q: The inner scale counts counterclockwise from the right arm, so the counterclockwise angle is 60°. What is the clockwise angle from the right arm to the other arm?
items.e: The two angles add up to 360°: 360° − 60° = 300°. (120° is the outer scale reading, which is a different angle.)

items.q: Jayden faces north. He turns 90° clockwise. Which way is he facing now?
items.e: Clockwise goes north → east → south → west. A quarter turn (90°) clockwise from north is east. West would be a quarter turn counterclockwise.
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 35° = 325°. (145° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: A turn of x counterclockwise and a turn of 3x clockwise go from the same arm to the same arm. What is x?
items.e: The two turns add up to 360°: x + 3x = 4x = 360°, so x = 90°. (45° comes from using 180°.)
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 230° = 130°.

items.q: The clockwise angle and the counterclockwise angle between the same two arms always add up to …
items.e: Turning one way and then the other way between the same two arms makes one full turn: 360°.
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 70° = 290°. (110° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

The arrow turns the opposite way to the hands of a clock, so it is counterclockwise. It goes past a straight angle, so it is reflex: about 250°. The clockwise angle between the same arms is about 110°.
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 100° = 260°. (80° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: The clockwise angle between two arms is 185°. What is the counterclockwise angle between the same arms?
items.e: 360° − 185° = 175°. It is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse. (5° comes from 185° − 180°.)

items.q: A turn of 120° counterclockwise ends in the same place as a clockwise turn of …
items.e: The two turns add up to 360°. 360° − 120° = 240° clockwise. (60° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: A clock hand points at 12. If it turned counterclockwise to 4, how many degrees would it turn?
items.e: Each hour space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. Clockwise from 12 to 4 is 4 × 30° = 120°. Counterclockwise is the other way around: 360° − 120° = 240°.

items.q: The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between two arms are equal. How big is each one?
items.e: They add up to 360°, and they are equal: 360° ÷ 2 = 180°. The two arms make a straight line.
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 270° = 90°.
The clockwise and counterclockwise angles between the same two arms add up to a full turn, 360°. 360° − 145° = 215°. (35° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: In a circle graph, the section for “soccer” makes an angle of 120° at the centre. What fraction of the circle is it?
items.e: 120° out of 360°: 360° ÷ 120° = 3, so it is one third. (One half would be 180°, and one quarter 90°.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go around a full turn, 360°, so each space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: On pizza day, a round pizza is cut into 8 equal slices from the centre. Sofia eats 3 slices. What angle at the centre do the slices that are left make?
items.e: Each slice is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. 5 slices are left: 5 × 45° = 225°, a reflex angle. (135° is the 3 slices that were eaten.)

items.q: A ship sails east. It turns 45° counterclockwise. Which way is it sailing now?
items.e: Counterclockwise from east turns toward north. 45° is half of a right angle, so the ship points halfway between east and north: northeast. (Southeast would be 45° clockwise.)

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn in 20 minutes?
items.e: The minute hand turns 360° in 60 minutes, so 6° each minute. 20 × 6° = 120°. (240° is the other 40 minutes.)

items.q: A classroom door is opened so that it makes an angle of 100° with the wall. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 100° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: In a circle graph, the section for “hockey” is one quarter of the circle. What angle does it make at the centre?
items.e: A full circle is 360°. One quarter of 360° is 360° ÷ 4 = 90°. (25° confuses a quarter with 25%.)

items.q: Olivia measures the slope of a ski hill with a protractor and writes 155°, but the slope is clearly acute. What is the angle?
items.e: An acute angle is less than 90°. Olivia read the wrong scale: 180° − 155° = 25°.

items.q: What is the reflex angle between the hands of a clock at 2 o’clock?
items.e: The smaller angle is 2 × 30° = 60°. The reflex angle goes the other way around: 360° − 60° = 300°.

items.q: At the skating rink, Priya spins 3 full turns. How many degrees does she turn?
items.e: One full turn is 360°. 3 × 360° = 1080°. (540° comes from using 180° for a full turn.)

items.q: Mateo is canoeing at the cottage, facing west. He turns the canoe 90° counterclockwise. Which way is he facing now?
items.e: Counterclockwise from west goes to south (north → west → south → east). North would be 90° clockwise.

items.q: Aiden writes code for a sprite that turns left (counterclockwise) 60°. What right (clockwise) turn would end in the same direction?
items.e: The two turns add up to 360°: 360° − 60° = 300° clockwise. (120° comes from 180° − 60°.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 10 o’clock?
items.e: From 10 to 12 is 2 hour spaces. Each space is 30°, so 2 × 30° = 60°. (300° is the reflex angle the other way around.)

items.q: At the skatepark, a skateboarder does a “180”: the board turns 180°. What angle is that?
items.e: 180° is half of a full turn (360°): a straight angle. The skateboarder ends up facing the other way.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn from 7:15 a.m. to 7:45 a.m.?
items.e: 30 minutes is half an hour, so half a turn: 360° ÷ 2 = 180°, a straight angle.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn from 3:00 p.m. to 3:45 p.m.?
items.e: 45 minutes is three quarters of an hour, so three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°, a reflex angle.

items.q: In coding class, Nathan’s robot faces north and turns 90° clockwise three times. What counterclockwise turn would get it to the same direction?
items.e: 3 × 90° = 270° clockwise. Clockwise and counterclockwise turns that end in the same place add up to 360°: 360° − 270° = 90° counterclockwise.

items.q: A lawn sprinkler waters while it turns 150° counterclockwise. What angle around the sprinkler does it not water?
items.e: The watered angle and the dry angle make a full turn: 360° − 150° = 210°. (30° comes from 180° − 150°.)

items.q: Maya spins one and a half full turns on the ice. How many degrees is that?
items.e: One full turn is 360°, and half a turn is 180°. 360° + 180° = 540°. (450° is 360° + 90°, a turn and a quarter.)

items.q: A wind turbine has 3 blades spaced equally around the centre. What is the angle between two blades next to each other?
items.e: The 3 equal angles go all the way around: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (60° comes from 180° ÷ 3.)
